title: To extend the Undertaking Spam, Spyware, And Fraud Enforcement With Enforcers beyond Borders Act of 2006, and for other purposes.
official_summary: This bill reauthorizes through FY2027 the U.S. SAFE WEB Act of 2006, which permits the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to take certain actions to protect consumers from cross-border fraud and deception occurring over the internet. The bill further requires the FTC to report on its activities concerning cross-border, online fraud and provide any policy recommendations to address such fraud.

summary.headline: Extends the FTC's authority to fight internet fraud that crosses national borders through fiscal year 2027 and requires the agency to report on that work.
summary.what_it_does: The law extends the U.S. SAFE WEB Act of 2006 through fiscal year 2027. That Act lets the Federal Trade Commission take certain actions against online fraud and deception that involve other countries. The law also requires the FTC to report on its cross-border online fraud work and to recommend policy changes to address it.

who_it_affects.group: Consumers who shop or do business online with people or companies in other countries
who_it_affects.how: The FTC keeps its authority to act against cross-border online fraud and deception that could affect them.
The agency's cross-border enforcement authority is extended, and it must prepare a report with policy recommendations on online fraud.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on October 20, 2020, and the extended authority runs through fiscal year 2027.
